item.title: Seafarer's union official says crews offered big money to transit Strait of Hormuz
item.description: As attacks continue to mount on shipping vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz, a seafarer's union official says some crews are being offered big rewards for making the crossing.

item.title: Harrowing accounts of violence and sex abuse in women's prison told in new podcast
item.description: Madi Bolanos and Anna Sussman's new podcast We Are Jane Doe, by KQED and Snap Studios, investigates rampant sex abuse at the Central California Women's Facility in Chowchilla, Ca.

item.title: She was a global star: Teen bikes 700 miles carrying injured dad. Where is she now?
item.description: Her epic ride — carrying her injured dad on her $20 hot pink bicycle — made headlines. Promises were made — financial help, training for a cycling career, even a movie deal. Were any of them kept?

item.title: Passenger terminal at Riyadh airport is struck again, a day after 12 were killed
item.description: A projectile struck a passenger terminal at the international airport in Riyadh on Sunday, a day after a missile hit the same terminal and killed 12 people, officials said.

item.description: A reenactment of the Battle of Hastings, which took place almost a millennium ago, is drawing crowds of enthusiasts in the UK.

item.title: Trump weighs joining the fight against Houthis after Riyadh airport attack
item.description: The surge in attacks, including against other Saudi airports, military facilities and oil infrastructure, has come in the week since a Saudi-led coalition launched a major military offensive against the Houthis.

item.title: Protests against voter roll revisions rock capital of world's largest democracy
item.description: Parts of the capital city of India, the world's largest democracy, are on lockdown. Protests over sweeping revisions to the voter rolls were met with a massive police crackdown.

item.title: U.S. and Russia tout diesel deal to ease sanctions and reopen fuel flows
item.description: Moscow and Washington tout a diesel deal to ease sanctions and reopen fuel flows, but few details leave questions on price impacts and U.S. policy, sparking anger from Ukraine and allies.
